questions.question: A earns ₹88 per hour and works for 10 hours. B earns ₹95 per hour and works for 8 hours. The ratio of per day wages of A to B is:
questions.solution:

A earns ₹88 per hour and works for 10 hours.

B earns ₹95 per hour and works for 8 hours.

**Formula Used:**

The ratio of per day wages of A to B = (Per day earnings of A) : (Per day earnings of B).

**Calculation:**

Per day earnings of A = ₹88 × 10

⇒ Per day earnings of A = ₹880

Per day earnings of B = ₹95 × 8

⇒ Per day earnings of B = ₹760

The ratio of per day wages of A to B = ₹880 : ₹760

⇒ The ratio of per day wages of A to B = 880 / 760

⇒ The ratio of per day wages of A to B = 22 : 19

**Therefore, the ratio of per day wages of A to B is 22 : 19.**

questions.question: Water in a conical flask with radius 7 cm and height 48 cm is poured into a cylindrical flask with radius 14 cm. The water level in the cylindrical flask is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of the conical flask (r₁) = 7 cm

Height of the conical flask (h₁) = 48 cm

Radius of the cylindrical flask (r₂) = 14 cm

We need to find the water level (height) in the cylindrical flask when the water from the conical flask is poured into it.

**Formula used:**

Volume of a cone = (1/3) × π × r₁² × h₁

Volume of a cylinder = π × r₂² × h₂, where h₂ is the height of water in the cylindrical flask.

**Calculations:**

Volume of water in the conical flask = (1/3) × π × r₁² × h₁ = (1/3) × π × (7)² × 48 = (1/3) × π × 49 × 48 = (1/3) × π × 2352 = 784π cm³.

Volume of water in the cylindrical flask = π × r₂² × h₂ = π × (14)² × h₂ = π × 196 × h₂ = 196π × h₂ cm³.

Since the water is poured from the conical flask to the cylindrical flask, the volumes are equal:

784π = 196π × h₂

784 = 196 × h₂

h₂ = 784 / 196 = 4 cm.

**∴ The water level in the cylindrical flask is 4 cm.**

questions.question: John has scored 60% in statistics and 70% in mathematics. A weightage of 2 is given to statistics and a weightage of 4 is given to mathematics. Which of the following expressions represents the weighted average of the two scores?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Score in Statistics = 60%

Score in Mathematics = 70%

Weightage for Statistics = 2

Weightage for Mathematics = 4

**Formula Used:**

Weighted Average = (Sum of Weighted Scores) / (Sum of Weights)

**Calculation:**

Weighted Scores:

Statistics Weighted Score = 2 × 60%

Mathematics Weighted Score = 4 × 70%

Sum of Weighted Scores = (2 × 60%) + (4 × 70%)

Sum of Weights = 2 + 4

Weighted Average = (Sum of Weighted Scores) / (Sum of Weights)

⇒ Weighted Average = [(2 × 60%) + (4 × 70%)] / (2 + 4)

**Correct Option:** Option 4

Cost of ingredient X = ₹80 per 5 gm

Cost of ingredient Y = ₹80 per 10 gm

Total weight of the mixture = 60 gm

Cost of the resulting mixture = ₹14 per gm

**Formula Used:**

Total cost of the mixture = Total weight × Cost per gram

Let the quantity of ingredient X = x gm, then quantity of Y = (60 - x) gm

Total cost of the mixture = Cost of X + Cost of Y

Cost of X = (x × 80) / 5

Cost of Y = ((60 - x) × 80) / 10

**Calculation:**

questions.question: A hemispherical bowl of internal radius 24 cm contains liquid. The liquid is to be filled into cylindrical container of diameter 8 cm and height 12 cm. What is the number of containers that are necessary to empty the bowl?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Internal radius of the hemispherical bowl = 24 cm

Diameter of the cylindrical container = 8 cm, so radius = 8 / 2 = 4 cm

Height of the cylindrical container = 12 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a hemisphere = (2 / 3) × π × r³

Volume of a cylinder = π × r² × h

Number of containers required = Volume of the hemisphere / Volume of one cylinder

**Calculation:**

Volume of the hemispherical bowl:

⇒ Volume = (2 / 3) × π × 24³

⇒ Volume = (2 / 3) × (22 / 7) × 24 × 24 × 24

⇒ Volume = (2 × 22 × 13824) / (3 × 7)

⇒ Volume = 608256 / 21

⇒ Volume ≈ 28964.57 cm³

Volume of one cylindrical container:

⇒ Volume = π × r² × h

⇒ Volume = (22 / 7) × 4 × 4 × 12

⇒ Volume = (22 × 192) / 7

⇒ Volume ≈ 604.57 cm³

Number of containers required:

⇒ Number = Volume of hemisphere / Volume of one cylinder

⇒ Number = 28964.57 / 604.57

⇒ Number ≈ 48

**The number of containers required to empty the bowl is 48.**

questions.solution:

Speed of Rohit = 5.4 km/h

Time taken = 40 minutes

New speed = 8 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculation:**

First, calculate the distance between Rohit's home and school:

Time taken = 40 minutes = 40 / 60 hours = 2/3 hours

Distance = Speed × Time

⇒ Distance = 5.4 × (2/3)

⇒ Distance = 3.6 km

Now, calculate the time taken at the new speed:

Time = Distance / Speed

⇒ Time = 3.6 / 8

⇒ Time = 0.45 hours

⇒ Time = 0.45 × 60 minutes

⇒ Time = 27 minutes

**∴ Rohit will take 27 minutes to reach his school if he walks at 8 km/h.**

questions.question: In which of the following classical dance forms are the actors' faces painted to symbolise the type of character they are playing?

questions.question: As per the Constitution (Ninety-First Amendment) Act, 2003, the total number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, shall NOT exceed:

options.text: 20% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
15% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
10% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
25% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Constitution (Ninety-First Amendment) Act, 2003** was enacted to prevent the proliferation of ministers and maintain efficiency in governance.
 
• According to this amendment, the total number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the **Union Council of Ministers**, shall not exceed **15% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha**.
 
• This limit applies to both the Union and State Councils of Ministers, as per **Articles 75 and 164** of the Constitution.
 
• The amendment was introduced to curb unnecessary expansion of ministries, which often led to inefficiency and misuse of public funds.
 
• The limit ensures a streamlined executive branch, fostering accountability and good governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Background of the 91st Amendment:**

 
 
• Before this amendment, there were no constitutional limits on the size of the Council of Ministers, leading to frequent cabinet expansions.
 
• The amendment was introduced following recommendations from the **National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (NCRWC)**.
 
 
 
• **Article 75:**
 
 
• Under Article 75(1A), the 91st Amendment added a clause limiting the size of the Union Council of Ministers.
 
• This restriction applies to the total membership of the Council, including the Prime Minister.
 
 
 
• **State-Level Provisions:**
 
 
• Article 164(1A) imposes a similar 15% cap on the size of the State Council of Ministers, based on the total number of members in the Legislative Assembly.
 
• A minimum of 12 ministers is permitted in smaller states to ensure effective governance.
 
 
 
• **Anti-Defection Measures:**
 
 
• The 91st Amendment also strengthened anti-defection provisions by disqualifying defectors from holding ministerial office.
 
• It removed the provision allowing defections by a one-third split in a party, making the two-thirds merger rule mandatory.

questions.question: In a metro station, it was observed that on an average 20 people per minute were using the escalator to reach at a height of 15 metres. Calculate the power of the escalator assuming the average mass of people to be 50 kg and acceleration due to gravity to be 10 m/s².
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2: 2.5 kW**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The escalator raises 20 people per minute to a height of 15 metres. Each person has an average mass of 50 kg.
 
• The gravitational force acting on each person is calculated as **weight = mass × gravity**, which is 50 kg × 10 m/s² = 500 N.
 
• The work done to raise one person is **work = force × height**, which is 500 N × 15 m = 7500 J.
 
• For 20 people, the total work done per minute is 7500 J × 20 = 150,000 J.
 
• Power is calculated as **power = work done / time**. Since time is 60 seconds (1 minute), the power of the escalator is 150,000 J / 60 s = 2500 W or 2.5 kW.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Work:** In physics, work is defined as the product of force applied and displacement in the direction of the force. It is measured in joules (J).
 
• **Power:** Power is the rate at which work is done or energy is transferred. The unit of power is watts (W), where 1 watt = 1 joule/second.
 
• **Gravitational Force:** The force exerted by gravity on an object is calculated as mass × acceleration due to gravity (g), which is approximately 9.8 m/s² but rounded to 10 m/s² for simplification.
 
• **Energy Conversion:** In machines like escalators, mechanical energy is used to lift objects or people against gravity, converting electrical energy into mechanical energy.
 
• **Efficiency:** Practical escalators may have less efficiency due to friction and other factors, but theoretical calculations assume ideal conditions.

questions.question: In Dholavira, which of the following materials is extensively used as a building material?
questions.solution:

• Dholavira, one of the most prominent archaeological sites of the Indus Valley Civilization, extensively utilized **stone** as a primary building material.
 
• The city’s structures, including walls, reservoirs, and gateways, were constructed using locally available stone, especially **sandstone and limestone**.
 
• Unlike other Harappan sites that predominantly used bricks, Dholavira is unique for its reliance on stone due to its geographical location in the arid region of Gujarat.
 
• The use of stone ensured durability and adaptability to the harsh climate of the Rann of Kutch, where Dholavira is located.
 
• The site’s sophisticated water management system, including reservoirs and drains, was also carved from stone, showcasing advanced engineering techniques of the Harappan people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dholavira:**

 
 
• Dholavira is located in the Rann of Kutch, Gujarat, and is one of the largest Harappan settlements in India.
 
• It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, recognized for its unique urban planning and water conservation systems.
 
 
 
• **Water Management System:**
 
 
• Dholavira is famous for its intricate water management system, including reservoirs, step wells, and drains.
 
• This system reflects the ingenuity of the Harappan civilization in adapting to a water-scarce environment.
 
 
 
• **Harappan Architecture:**
 
 
• The Harappan civilization is known for its urban planning, including grid-patterned streets, drainage systems, and standardized building materials like bricks and stones.
 
 
 
• **Materials Used in Harappan Sites:**
 
 
• While baked and unbaked bricks were common in most Harappan sites, Dholavira stands out for its extensive use of stone due to the availability of local resources.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Australia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The concept of the **Concurrent List** in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the **Australian Constitution**.
 
• In the **Australian federal system**, powers are divided between the federal and state governments, with concurrent powers allowing both levels of government to legislate on certain subjects.
 
• The Indian Constitution adopts this idea to allocate legislative powers between the Union and State legislatures under **Article 246** and the **Seventh Schedule**.
 
• The Concurrent List in India contains subjects on which both the Parliament and State Legislatures can legislate, but in case of a conflict, the Union law prevails (as per **Article 254**).
 
• Examples of subjects in the Concurrent List include education, forest, trade unions, and marriage laws.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution**:

 
 
• The Seventh Schedule divides legislative powers between the Union and State governments into three lists: **Union List, State List, and Concurrent List**.
 
• The Union List contains 100 subjects, the State List has 61 subjects, and the Concurrent List has 52 subjects as of the latest amendment.
 
 
 
• **Article 246**:
 
 
• It lays down the distribution of legislative powers between the Union and the States.
 
• Parliament has exclusive power to make laws on subjects in the Union List, while State Legislatures have exclusive power on the State List.
 
 
 
• **Article 254**:
 
 
• In case of a conflict between Union and State laws on a Concurrent List subject, the law made by the Union Parliament will prevail.
 
• However, a state law can prevail if it has received the President's assent.
 
 
 
• **Federal Features of the Indian Constitution**:
 
 
• Indian federalism is unique, combining the division of powers with a strong unitary bias.
 
• Features like a strong central government, single citizenship, and a unified judiciary distinguish it from purely federal systems like the USA.

questions.question: The climatic diversity of India is characterised by its distinctiveness, and one of the following factors does NOT contribute to it is ____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1 (Longitudinal extent)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Longitudinal extent** does not significantly influence climatic diversity in India as it mainly determines the local time differences across the country, rather than climatic variations.
 
• The climate variations across India are majorly influenced by factors like latitude, altitude, distance from the sea, and geographical features such as mountains and plateaus.
 
• India’s latitudinal extent (between 8° N and 37° N) contributes to the climatic diversity by placing the country in both tropical and subtropical zones.
 
• Topography, including the Himalayas and the Thar Desert, plays a critical role in influencing climatic patterns, such as monsoons and regional temperature differences.
 
• Vegetation impacts local climates by affecting moisture levels, temperature regulation, and precipitation patterns, contributing to India’s climatic diversity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Latitude and Climate:**

 
 
• India’s latitudinal extent ensures climatic zones ranging from tropical in the south to subtropical and temperate in the north.
 
• Regions near the Equator experience higher temperatures and greater humidity compared to regions farther north.
 
 
 
• **Role of Topography:**
 
 
• The Himalayas prevent cold Central Asian winds from entering India, contributing to the tropical climate in most parts of the country.
 
• Western Ghats and coastal areas experience high rainfall due to orographic rainfall during monsoons.
 
 
 
• **Vegetation and Climate:**
 
 
• Dense forests in regions like the Western Ghats and Northeast India contribute to higher rainfall and cooler climates.
 
• Deforestation in some areas has led to changes in local climates, including increased aridity and temperature.
 
 
 
• **Longitude and Time Zones:**
 
 
• The longitudinal extent of India (68°7' E to 97°25' E) results in a time difference of nearly 2 hours between its eastern and western extremities.
 
• However, longitude has minimal impact on climatic diversity as it does not directly influence temperature, precipitation, or seasonal patterns.

• **Flame cells** are specialized excretory cells found in flatworms, such as Planaria, belonging to the phylum Platyhelminthes.
 
• These cells play a crucial role in the removal of nitrogenous waste products and maintaining osmotic balance in flatworms.
 
• Flame cells are part of the **protonephridial system**, which functions as the excretory system in these organisms.
 
• The name "flame cell" is derived from the flickering movement of cilia present inside the cell, resembling a flame.
 
• The cilia in flame cells drive the waste materials and excess water out of the body through excretory pores.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• This system consists of a network of tubules and flame cells that facilitate excretion and osmoregulation in flatworms.
 
• It is considered a primitive excretory structure compared to advanced systems in higher organisms.
 
 
 
• **Flatworms (Platyhelminthes):**
 
 
• Flatworms are bilaterally symmetrical, dorsoventrally flattened, and lack a circulatory system.
 
• They rely on diffusion for nutrient and gas exchange, making their excretory system essential for waste removal.
 
 
 
• **Cnidoblast Cells:**
 
 
• These are specialized cells found in cnidarians (e.g., jellyfish) and are used for defense and prey capture, not excretion.
 
 
 
• **Osmoregulation in Flatworms:**
